question.text: In the FIU-IND case against Bybit Fintech Limited, what was the primary nature of the compliance violation?

answer.text: Failure to register with FIU-IND as a reporting entity and non-compliance with obligations under PMLA including record maintenance and suspicious transaction reporting
Failure to obtain a banking license from the Reserve Bank of India before commencing operations
Charging excessive transaction fees to customers without proper disclosure
Unauthorized trading in equity derivatives without SEBI registration

explanation.text: The Logic: Bybit, as a Virtual Digital Asset Service Provider classified as a reporting entity, was penalized Rs 9.27 crore for expanding services without FIU-IND registration and for violations of Section 12(1) of PMLA read with the PML Rules, including obligations around record maintenance and suspicious transaction reporting. The Trap: Option B (banking license from RBI) conflates banking regulation with AML compliance. Bybit's violation was about PMLA obligations as a reporting entity, not about banking licensure. Options C and D describe unrelated regulatory issues. Note: Virtual Digital Asset Service Providers are classified as reporting entities — FIU-IND registration and full PMLA compliance are mandatory, as the Bybit case demonstrates with its substantial penalty.
